answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a haven as the anchor of the cost.
